title: When Did the Sooner Schooner Debut? The 1964 Story Behind OU's Wagon
question: When did the Sooner Schooner first appear at an Oklahoma football game?
answer: The Sooner Schooner made its first appearance at Owen Field on September 26, 1964, when USC beat Oklahoma 40-14. The covered wagon and its ponies became an official OU mascot in 1980.
summary: The Sooner Schooner debuted at Owen Field on Sept. 26, 1964, versus USC and became OU's official mascot in 1980. Here is how the wagon tradition began.
body: Few sights in college football say Oklahoma quite like a small covered wagon tearing across Owen Field after a Sooner score. That tradition began on September 26, 1964, in the first home game of the Gomer Jones era. The debut did not go to plan on the scoreboard, as Southern California rolled to a 40-14 win in front of a sellout crowd of 61,700.

The wagon and ponies were a gift from two Sapulpa brothers, Dr. M.S. Bartlett and Charley F. "Buzz" Bartlett, both former OU students. Dr. Bartlett modeled the wagon on the prairie schooner his parents used when they settled in northeastern Oklahoma, and the brothers wanted a mascot that symbolized the settling of Oklahoma Territory and the pioneering spirit of the 89ers. The original pair were three-year-old Shetland ponies, and in that first season the rig stayed behind the end zone because officials worried about damage to the field.

Freshman RUF/NEK Mick Cottom of Liberty Mounds earned the honor of being the first to drive the Schooner across Owen Field. The RUF/NEKS have driven the wagon for decades since, and in 2020 Darby Dean of the RUF/NEK Lil' Sis became the first woman to drive it during a game.

The university's Board of Regents made the Schooner an official mascot in 1980, and in 1981 Dr. Bartlett signed the trademark rights over to OU for one dollar. The ponies, named Boomer and Sooner, are Welsh ponies today, and the wagon and team have been cared for by the university since 2011. More than six decades in, the Schooner still serves as a quick history lesson every time Oklahoma puts points on the board.
